item.title: Actively Exploited Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-104935 Drives Urgent Patching
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Oct 10:00 → 14 Oct 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

CISA warns admins to immediately fix Ivanti flaw exploited as zero-day — Must Read

CISA urges organizations to immediately patch Ivanti Connect Secure for CVE-2026-104935, a high-severity zero-day authentication bypass actively exploited to enable unauthenticated command execution, credential theft, and data exfiltration. Suspected compromises require forensic investigation and may warrant a factory reset, upgrade, and credential rotation.

  • CISA urged organizations to immediately patch CVE-2026-104935, an actively exploited Ivanti Connect Secure authentication-bypass flaw that enables unauthenticated remote command execution.
  • Ivanti released Connect Secure versions 22.8R2.5, 25.1.3.0, 25.1.3.1, and 25.1.1.2 to address the flaw and said exploitation in the wild is limited.
  • Volexity reported that threat actor UTA0576 chained the authentication bypass with remote code execution and privilege escalation flaws to obtain unauthenticated root-level code execution.
  • CISA said attackers have used the zero-day to steal credentials and exfiltrate data, while Volexity observed targeting of Active Directory secrets including LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys.
  • CISA advised organizations that find a compromised appliance to back up its configuration, factory-reset and update it, restore the configuration, and reset credentials, certificates, API keys, and license-server credentials.

Technologies: vpn, remote-access

Products: ivanti-connect-secure, integrity-checker-tool

Vendors: ivanti

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-103849) Adobe Commerce Template Injection Remote Code Execution — Must Read

Adobe has patched CVE-2026-103849, a critical unauthenticated template-injection flaw (CVSS 10.0) that allows remote code execution in Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, and Magento Open Source. Organizations should urgently update every production and staging storefront to the October 2026 dated releases, as external scans cannot reliably distinguish patched from vulnerable builds.

  • CVE-2026-103849 is a CVSS 10.0 template-injection flaw that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution in Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, and Magento Open Source.
  • Adobe released fixes in security bulletin APSB26-153 on 13 October 2026, with affected organizations instructed to install the October 2026 dated releases for their product line.
  • A store’s major version alone cannot establish whether it is vulnerable, because the dated September builds are affected while the corresponding October builds are fixed.
  • CyCognito found that roughly one in six observed storefronts had staging, test, QA, or demo markers, and these internet-facing environments may run the same codebase as production.
  • The article recommends inventorying all production and non-production instances, checking payment and checkout pages for unauthorized scripts, and reviewing admin accounts, API keys, and integration tokens for unexpected changes.

Technologies: cms

Products: adobe-commerce, adobe-commerce-b2b, magento-open-source, cycognito-platform

Vendors: adobe, cycognito

Global takedown hits network behind 1 billion phishing messages — Must Read

A global law-enforcement operation disrupted YAM Store and associated phishing kits CoGUI and Iron Man, which facilitated more than a billion phishing messages targeting organizations worldwide. Microsoft disabled over 20,000 linked accounts and blocked 100,000 fraudulent domains used to impersonate organizations and steal credentials and payment data.

  • A global investigation disrupted YAM Store, an underground marketplace linked to the CoGUI, Haozi, and Iron Man System phishing kits, collectively tracked as Storm-2990.
  • Microsoft said the phishing platforms sent more than 750 million malicious email and text messages to Microsoft customers since the start of the year, while the broader ecosystem facilitated more than one billion messages targeting over 75,000 organizations in 150 countries.
  • YAM Store sold compromised or fraudulently obtained Microsoft and Google accounts, licenses, and storage, including accounts acquired using expired domains or fake organizations created with AI tools.
  • The phishing kits used lures such as unpaid tolls, traffic penalties, delivery problems, and account verification requests, while also using location restrictions, fake human-verification pages, and IP filtering to hinder analysis.
  • Under a U.S. court order, Microsoft and Health-ISAC seized and redirected supporting domains, deactivated more than 20,000 YAM Store-linked accounts, and blocked 100,000 domains used for impersonation and fraud.

Technologies: cloud-platform, object-storage, iam

Products: microsoft-365, sharepoint, onedrive

Vendors: microsoft, google

curl Patches HTTP/2 Upload Flaw After PoC Demonstrates Client-Side Code Execution — Should Read

curl and libcurl 8.12.0–8.22.0 contain a high-severity HTTP/2 upload use-after-free flaw (CVE-2026-92392) that a malicious upload server could potentially turn into client-side code execution. Upgrade to curl 8.23.0 or a listed backported release, or disable HTTP/2 until patched.

  • curl fixed CVE-2026-92392 in version 8.23.0, a high-severity use-after-free flaw affecting curl and libcurl versions 8.12.0 through 8.22.0.
  • A malicious server receiving an HTTP/2 upload can trigger the flaw, and the public proof of concept demonstrated code execution on the uploading client under highly specific conditions.
  • The attack requires an upload of roughly 135 KB to an attacker-controlled server whose certificate passes the client’s checks, with HTTP/2 enabled and negotiated.
  • Users should upgrade to curl 8.23.0 or an available backported fixed release; until then, curl recommends avoiding HTTP/2 by using HTTP/1.1.
  • The public report credited Luna Tong of Anthropic, and curl said Anthropic’s OSS Scanner identified the issue.

Products: curl, libcurl, oss-scanner, claude, rock-solid-curl

Vendors: curl-project, anthropic, debian

Researchers Used a Public OpenAI Model to Build a $250,000 Chrome Full-Chain Exploit in Six Days — Should Read

XBOW researchers used OpenAI’s public GPT-5.6 Sol model to help build a three-bug Chrome-for-Windows exploit chain in six days, earning Google’s $250,000 maximum reward. Google has patched the flaws, so Chrome users should restart and update to version 152.0.7977.82 or later.

  • XBOW researchers used AI agents running OpenAI's publicly available GPT-5.6 Sol model to build a Chrome-for-Windows exploit chain in six days.
  • The chain combined three previously unknown Chrome flaws to let a web page run code outside Chrome on a Windows computer without requiring a click or download.
  • Google confirmed and fixed all three flaws and paid XBOW its maximum $250,000 reward for a full Chrome exploit chain.
  • XBOW said the six-day effort cost about $40,000 in AI charges, although it followed months of earlier work and an earlier full-chain effort that took two months.
  • Chrome users need to restart the browser after updating so that version 152.0.7977.82 or later takes effect.

Technologies: browser, operating-system

Products: google-chrome, gpt-5-6-sol, v8, crashpad, windows

Vendors: google, xbow, openai

Hirudo Android Trojan Uses Patched Banking Apps to Bypass Their Built-In Security Checks — Should Read

ThreatFabric uncovered Hirudo, an Android banking trojan distributed through fake app updates that steals credentials and remotely controls devices. Its key advance is replacing legitimate Indonesian banking apps with tampered copies that bypass in-app signature, accessibility, screen-capture, and Play Integrity checks.

  • ThreatFabric identified Hirudo, an Android banking trojan delivered through shopping, adult video, and entertainment dropper apps that present a fake in-app update to install the payload.
  • Hirudo can steal credentials, SMS messages, screen and camera data, and enable live remote control of an infected device.
  • The operation includes patched replacements for eight Indonesian banking apps, which are installed after the genuine app is removed.
  • The altered banking apps use a hooking engine to return deceptive results for signature, accessibility, screen-capture, and Play Integrity checks.
  • ThreatFabric said Hirudo campaigns use fake Google Play Store-style web pages and may direct users there through advertisements on Meta-owned social media platforms.

Technologies: mobile-os

Products: android, google-play-protect, google-play-integrity-api, mediaprojection

Vendors: threatfabric, google, meta

Break the silence: Kazakhstan-nexus UAT-6275 targets CIS government organizations — Should Read

Cisco Talos and Recorded Future linked UAT-6275 (TAG-193/Silent Lynx), a suspected Kazakhstan-nexus espionage group, to campaigns targeting government, environmental, and energy organizations across Central Asia and the CIS. The group uses malicious documents, PowerShell downloaders, GitHub-hosted payloads, and a WinRAR exploit to deploy reverse shells and maintain access.

  • Cisco Talos and Recorded Future identified UAT-6275, also tracked as TAG-193, targeting government organizations across Central Asia and the wider Commonwealth of Independent States.
  • The group used four delivery chains involving macro-enabled Word documents, PowerShell-based downloaders, GitHub-hosted scripts, and a WinRAR archive exploiting CVE-2025-8088.
  • Recovered payloads included the Chvost, Laplas, and PickleShell reverse shells, which provide interactive remote access on compromised systems.
  • Three publicly accessible staging directories and a GitHub repository exposed payload builds, tool inventories, and changes to the group’s command-and-control infrastructure.
  • Talos assessed with medium confidence that UAT-6275 has a Kazakhstan nexus based on infrastructure access, Russian-language artifacts, sample submissions, working-hour analysis, and regional targeting interests.

Technologies: source-control, waf

Products: github, winrar, fortiweb

Vendors: cisco, recorded-future, github, rarlab, fortinet

Congressional probe faults Match Group for failing to rein in dating app scams — Should Read

A U.S. congressional investigation found that Match Group failed to adequately prevent scammers from reaching users on Tinder and Hinge, with roughly 1.5 million bad actors matching with legitimate users in the first nine months of 2025. The report says outdated fraud-detection models and platform incentives amplified scammer visibility, while Match Group disputes aspects of the findings and cites newer biometric verification measures.

  • A U.S. Joint Economic Committee investigation found that nearly 1.5 million scammers and other bad actors on Tinder and Hinge matched with legitimate users during the first nine months of 2025.
  • The report said the median Tinder scammer's profile views increased by more than 700% from May 2024 to December 2025 and alleged that Tinder was more likely to show scammer or bad-actor profiles than regular-user profiles.
  • Investigators said internal Match Group documents showed that Tinder had not updated certain machine-learning models used to identify scammers for years, although a company official disputed that characterization.
  • Match Group said its Face Check video-selfie verification tool, rolled out across new Tinder accounts in October 2025, reduced U.S. user interactions with scam accounts by 70% in pilots.
  • The Senate unanimously passed bipartisan legislation last month that would require dating apps to notify people who interacted with a scammer, even after the scam account has been banned.

Products: tinder, hinge, match-com, plenty-of-fish, face-check

Vendors: match-group

Microsoft: Recent Windows updates may trigger Remote Desktop failures — Should Read

Microsoft says recent Windows 11 updates can cause Remote Desktop connections to fail with error 0xC000000D on enterprise-managed hosts when Administrator protection is enabled. Until a fix is released, IT administrators should disable Administrator protection through policy management.

  • Microsoft says non-admin users may be unable to connect through Remote Desktop after recent Windows updates when Administrator protection is enabled.
  • Remote Desktop connections can fail with error 0xC000000D and the message "The token that was passed to the function is invalid."
  • The issue primarily affects enterprise-managed remote devices used as Remote Desktop hosts on Windows 11 24H2, 25H2, 26H1, and 26H2.
  • Microsoft says Administrator protection is enabled by default in Windows 11 security baselines for versions 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2 unless an organization changed the policy.
  • Microsoft's temporary workaround is for IT administrators to disable Administrator protection through their policy-management method, such as by resetting the User Account Control Type Of Admin Approval Mode policy.

Technologies: operating-system, remote-access, iam, mfa

Products: windows-11, remote-desktop, remote-desktop-services, windows-hello, microsoft-intune, microsoft-security-compliance-toolkit

Vendors: microsoft

The Sign-In Link Pointed Home, and Home Was a Decoy — May Read

A phishing email used a legitimate Microsoft OAuth authorization endpoint and a fake, readable URL pointing to the victim’s own nonexistent subdomain to make the link appear trustworthy. Defenders should assess and hunt the OAuth client ID and app registration rather than trust URL-shaped query parameters such as uri.

  • A Teams-styled phishing email targeting a senior finance leader at a UK medical-device and infection-prevention manufacturer linked to the genuine Microsoft OAuth authorization endpoint.
  • The authorization link contained an unknown third-party OAuth client ID, prompt=none, identity and Microsoft Graph User.Read permissions, and a double-encoded uri parameter pointing to a nonexistent subdomain of the victim’s company.
  • The link omitted redirect_uri and response_type, which Microsoft documents as required parameters, while uri is not a documented Microsoft authorization parameter.
  • Microsoft filtering delivered the message despite passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and composite authentication checks and clean reputations for its Microsoft-hosted links.
  • IRONSCALES classified the email as VIP impersonation with 85 confidence and automatically quarantined the single affected mailbox, with no evidence that anyone clicked.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, email-security

Products: microsoft-entra-id, microsoft-teams, microsoft-graph, google-workspace, ironscales-themis

Vendors: microsoft, google, ironscales

Russian travel booking platform suspends reservations after cyberattack — May Read

Russian online travel agency Anywayanyday suspended new airline, train, and hotel bookings after a cyberattack disrupted its IT infrastructure, though it says existing reservations remain valid and there is no evidence of customer data compromise.

  • Russian online travel agency Anywayanyday temporarily suspended new bookings after a cyberattack on its IT infrastructure.
  • Customers cannot currently purchase airline or train tickets or book hotels through Anywayanyday, while previously confirmed reservations remain valid.
  • Anywayanyday said its website is unavailable as it restores systems and that it has found no evidence that customers' personal data was compromised.
  • The company did not identify the attackers, explain how its systems were breached, or provide a timeline for restoring normal service.
  • The incident occurs amid broader travel disruptions in Russia, where more than 500 flights serving Moscow have been delayed or canceled since Tuesday evening.

Products: anywayanyday

Vendors: anywayanyday

An AI Agent Found a Critical OTP Bypass in Production. The Attack Was the Easy Part. — May Read

In an authorized assessment, Reflectiz says its AI pentesting agent discovered that a major insurer’s login API could send one-time passcodes to an attacker-controlled email address, enabling account takeover with customer identifiers. The sponsored case study argues that continuous, context-aware agentic testing can uncover authentication flaws missed by periodic pentests.

  • During an authorized assessment of a major insurer’s production website, Reflectiz says its AI pentesting agent independently identified and confirmed a critical authentication bypass.
  • The login request allowed the delivery channel and destination for a one-time passcode to be changed, and the server sent an email code to the supplied address without verifying that it belonged to the account.
  • The agent analyzed the site’s JavaScript and API calls, then tested the suspected delivery-field manipulation through the live login flow and reached an authenticated state before its guardrails stopped the test.
  • Reflectiz says its agentic pentesting combines open-ended investigation with structured endpoint and attack-category testing, while a separate validator agent reproduces suspected findings before reporting them.
  • The article argues that recurring agentic testing can assess changing web applications more frequently than point-in-time pentests when the system has appropriate access and defined boundaries.

Technologies: mfa

Products: reflectiz-agentic-pentesting

Vendors: reflectiz

Package managers have an integrity problem — May Read

Testing of 25 popular package managers found that fewer than half verify lockfile integrity by default, and only Go verifies every downloaded package and signatures by default against a compromised repository. The article argues that stronger default verification using signed packages, identity-based signing, and transparency logs is needed to prevent repository-side supply-chain tampering.

  • A Docker and mitmproxy-based test harness evaluated 25 package managers by simulating a compromised package repository that injects malicious code into otherwise legitimate packages.
  • Fewer than half of the tested package managers used lockfiles that detect tampering by default, and only Go and vcpkg verified integrity for every downloaded package in the tested configurations.
  • Several package managers contain hashes in lockfiles but do not reliably enforce them by default; for example, Pub warns about a hash mismatch and updates the lockfile unless the non-default --enforce-lockfile option is used.
  • Package signatures are available in several ecosystems, but many package managers do not verify them during standard installation or require users to configure trusted signing keys and verification settings.
  • Go was the only tested package manager that verified signatures by default, using its checksum database and a public key hardcoded in Go’s source code to validate downloaded package contents.

Technologies: package-registry

5 Key Takeaways From Censys’ State of the Internet Report — Optional

Censys’ 2026 report finds that major Internet security risks often hide in overlooked assets, including exposed AI automation platforms, mobile-connected industrial systems, unpatched legacy software, and services running on nonstandard ports. Effective asset visibility across all networks and ports is critical because attackers can easily find exposures that organizations may not know they own.

  • Between October 2025 and July 2026, Internet-exposed hosts running AI-related tools grew by more than 63%, with n8n accounting for 113,926 exposed hosts.
  • Censys found that roughly 70% of hosts running industrial control system devices and services globally are consistently located on consumer and mobile networks, which can obscure ownership and complicate remediation.
  • The oldest exposed software versions changed very little over a 2.5-year period, persisting at small but stable levels despite broader software populations gradually updating.
  • The United States hosts 45.5% of observed web-based threats, while the report says threat actors select hosting providers mainly for cost and permissiveness rather than country.
  • Many Internet services run on non-standard ports, including 96% of SOCKS proxies, 68% of HTTP(S) services, and 34% of SSH services.

Products: n8n, censys-map-of-the-internet

How to Run a Deepfake Readiness Drill Before a Cloned Voice Calls Your Team — Optional

Organizations should run regular, controlled deepfake-readiness drills to test whether staff follow out-of-band verification procedures for urgent payment, MFA reset, and privileged-access requests. Because cloned voices and video can be convincing, reliable callback rules, dual approval, and blameless reporting matter more than detecting a fake by ear or sight.

  • Cloned voices and synthetic video calls can be used to request fraudulent payments, help desk MFA resets, or privileged account changes.
  • The article recommends verifying payment, banking, credential, MFA, and access-change requests through an independently sourced phone number rather than a number supplied in the request.
  • A deepfake readiness drill should use controlled scenarios and ensure that no real money can move and no real access can be granted.
  • Organizations should measure whether participants followed verification procedures, how quickly they escalated concerns, and where the process broke down.
  • The article recommends conducting drills at least twice a year and updating them when high-exposure personnel or organizational circumstances change.

Products: microsoft-teams

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft

The Week in Vulnerabilities: Toptech, Lantronix, Langflow, and CISA Malcolm Flaws — Optional

Cyble observed active exploitation of newly disclosed web and AI-platform flaws alongside persistent targeting of old IoT and embedded-networking bugs, while CISA issued 14 ICS advisories covering 54 vulnerabilities, including critical issues in fuel-management, router, camera, and charging-platform products.   • Cyble’s global sensors observed exploitation attempts against about 20 known vulnerabilities, including recently disclosed flaws in WordPress, Apache Solr, Langflow, and n8n as well as older embedded-device and router flaws.
  • CISA issued 14 industrial control system advisories covering 54 vulnerabilities, including 13 rated critical, across vendors such as Toptech Systems, Lantronix, VIVOTEK, MikroTik, Monta, Anjvision, Armatura, and CISA’s Malcolm platform.
  • Toptech Systems TMS7 and TopHAT contained multiple critical issues, including SQL injection, unrestricted file upload, and exposure of files to external parties; these products support liquid fuel and chemical distribution.
  • Cyble recorded a Mirai variant chaining CVE-2018-10561 and CVE-2018-10562 against Dasan GPON home routers, allowing unauthenticated remote command execution when the flaws are combined.
  • Cyble also observed phishing, brute-force activity against remote-access and database services, and malware families including CoinMiner, WannaCry, Mirai, IRCBot, Hajime, Gafgyt, and Wacatac.

item.title: CVE-2026-74580 Vghost Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Root and VM Escape
item.content:encoded:
Window: 14 Oct 06:00 → 14 Oct 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host — Should Read

CVE-2026-74580 (Vghost) is a Linux vhost flaw that can let local users gain root and, in certain virtualized configurations, allow a guest VM to compromise its host’s QEMU process. Organizations should install patched kernels and restrict access to /dev/vhost-net and /dev/vhost-vsock until patching is complete.

  • CVE-2026-74580, called Vghost, is a flaw in Linux’s vhost subsystem that can allow a local user to read and write kernel memory and gain root privileges.
  • In certain virtual-machine configurations using a virtual IOMMU and device-IOTLB mode, an untrusted guest can use the flaw to write outside intended memory in the host’s QEMU process.
  • The issue affects Linux kernels from version 4.11 through 7.2-rc4 and was reproduced on Ubuntu, RHEL, Amazon Linux, Microsoft Azure Linux, and Oracle Linux.
  • The upstream fix clears vhost’s memory-mapping cache whenever a virtual ring is reconfigured, and organizations should install a kernel containing commit de845981da67 and reboot.
  • Until systems are patched, the article recommends restricting access to /dev/vhost-net and /dev/vhost-vsock; only a patched kernel addresses the guest-to-host path.

Technologies: operating-system, hypervisor

Products: linux-kernel, vhost, qemu, red-hat-enterprise-linux, amazon-linux-2023, microsoft-azure-linux, oracle-linux, ubuntu

Vendors: tencent, linux-kernel-project, red-hat, amazon, microsoft, oracle, ubuntu, qemu-project

Introducing the NetSPI Platform MCP — Optional

NetSPI has launched a Model Context Protocol integration that lets AI clients such as Claude query live pentest findings, prioritize remediation, and draft code fixes and pull requests. The integration is intended to move vulnerability management from static reports into automated engineering workflows.

  • NetSPI introduced a Model Context Protocol integration that connects the NetSPI Platform to AI clients so users can query vulnerability findings in natural language.
  • The integration is presented as an alternative to relying solely on static PDF pentest reports, providing live insights for prioritizing and remediating findings.
  • In the example workflow, users ask an AI client for newly published project findings and then request prioritization with OWASP Top 10 categories and context.
  • NetSPI demonstrates using Claude Code to retrieve high-severity findings, locate the described issues in a codebase, and draft pull requests with descriptions of the changes.
  • The article suggests combining NetSPI Platform data with other workflows, including creating Jira tickets and providing project updates through Slack.

Beyond the Wallet: How Identity Intelligence Helps Investigators Uncover Crypto Crime — Optional

Constella promotes its identity intelligence data, including breach and infostealer-derived records, as a complement to TRM Labs' blockchain analytics for investigating crypto-enabled crime. The combined approach is intended to help investigators link wallet activity with digital identities while treating correlations as leads rather than proof of attribution.

  • Blockchain intelligence can help investigators trace cryptocurrency transactions, examine wallet relationships, and understand how funds move.
  • Identity intelligence can help investigators explore digital footprints around email addresses, usernames, credentials, and other data exposed through breaches, ransomware attacks, and infostealer infections.
  • Constella says its data can provide leads that investigators should assess alongside transaction evidence, account records, victim reports, and other case information rather than treating them as proof of identity or wrongdoing.
  • Stolen or exposed credentials may mean that an account linked to suspicious activity belongs to a victim or has been compromised, purchased, or shared rather than operated by a criminal.
  • Constella is participating as a data partner for TRM Labs' Orion launch, contributing identity intelligence intended to complement TRM's blockchain transaction and network analysis.

Organizations should prioritize the exploited Windows Shell bug and publicly disclosed .NET WDAC bypass, then use Microsoft's risk cohorts to triage the broader update set.

OpenAI engineer arrested for allegedly planting spy device in office — Should Read

A former OpenAI engineer was arrested after allegedly hiding encrypted audio-recording devices in executive conference rooms at the company’s San Francisco offices to capture confidential discussions. OpenAI said it fired the employee, referred the case to the FBI, and found no evidence that model weights, source code, or customer data were accessed or exfiltrated.

  • The U.S. Department of Justice announced that Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national who had worked at OpenAI since July 2025, was arrested on October 9 and charged with illegally intercepting oral communications.
  • OpenAI security personnel found a concealed recording device plugged into a USB port behind a television in an executive conference room on September 30.
  • The DOJ alleges that the device was installed around September 28, held encrypted data, and was concealed in toilet paper.
  • OpenAI said it terminated Alfozan and referred the incident to the FBI after using its AI models to help identify the employee allegedly responsible.
  • OpenAI stated that it had no indication that model weights, source code, or customer data had been accessed or removed.

Vendors: openai

The Noise Inside the Network: How an Unsophisticated Attack Exposed a Third-Party Risk — May Read

A European bank was compromised through a misconfigured third-party gateway and stolen credentials, enabling months of noisy network reconnaissance and password guessing. Cortex XDR stopped an attempted WSUS-based escalation, underscoring that MFA, prompt patching, and strong third-party access controls can prevent major incidents.

  • A European bank detected unauthorized VPN-based access attempts that had occurred over several months and engaged Unit 42 to investigate the intrusion.
  • The intrusion began through a third-party-managed external gateway appliance that was not configured to enforce strict authentication, using compromised credentials.
  • After entering the network, the attacker conducted broad scans, tested passwords against administrator accounts, and accessed internal documentation and data shares.
  • The attacker attempted to exploit a Windows Server Update Services remote-code-execution vulnerability on the bank’s central configuration management server.
  • Cortex XDR detected and contained the unauthorized code-execution attempt, and Unit 42’s subsequent forensic review found no additional attacker presence or persistent backdoors.

Technologies: xdr, siem, soar, operating-system

Ghostscript flaw lets hackers hijack servers via PDF uploads — Should Read

A critical Ghostscript heap-buffer-overflow flaw (CVE-2026-39919) can enable remote code execution when servers process specially crafted PDF uploads, including through WordPress thumbnail-generation chains using ImageMagick. Administrators should update Ghostscript to 10.08.0 or a backported fixed release, or disable PDF uploads/rendering until patched.

  • CVE-2026-39919 is a critical heap buffer overflow in Ghostscript that can allow remote code execution through specially crafted PDF files.
  • The flaw can be reached when systems process uploaded PDFs for previews or thumbnails, such as WordPress installations using PHP Imagick, ImageMagick, and Ghostscript.
  • Wordfence researchers developed proof-of-concept files that caused Ghostscript to write 1,024 bytes into a 256-byte buffer, but reliable code execution depended on the target environment.
  • Artifex fixed the issue in Ghostscript 10.08.0 and backported fixes to older versions.
  • Wordfence said it had not observed exploitation of CVE-2026-39919 in the wild.

Technologies: cms, container-platform

Products: ghostscript, argus, imagemagick, wordpress

Vendors: artifex, wordfence, imagemagick, wordpress, docker

Two arrested as DOJ takes down laptop farms responsible for $3 million in North Korean revenue — Should Read

The U.S. DOJ arrested two Americans and raided more than 40 Texas residences used as laptop farms that allegedly helped North Korean IT workers fraudulently earn over $3 million from about 70 U.S. companies. The FBI warns the scheme is expanding through stolen identities, U.S.-based facilitators, and subcontractors in South Asia and West Africa.

  • The U.S. Department of Justice raided more than 40 residences in Texas between September 21 and 25 and seized 187 laptops and other devices allegedly used in a North Korean remote IT-worker scheme.
  • The DOJ arrested Michael James Bostelle of Pennsylvania and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo of Texas on wire fraud, money laundering, and identity theft charges.
  • Prosecutors said Bostelle and Pena helped North Korean workers earn more than $3 million from roughly 70 U.S. companies in 17 states.
  • The FBI said North Korean IT workers increasingly use stolen identities, U.S.-based facilitators, and freelancers in South Asia and West Africa to obtain jobs and complete assignments.
  • The FBI warned that some North Korean workers have threatened physical violence or to release sensitive company data after their accounts were removed.

Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another — Should Read

Docker fixed GhostPat (CVE-2026-105445), a critical Docker Hub flaw that for more than two years could let attackers transfer their personal access tokens during account conversion and use them to push, pull, or delete registry images as another user. Docker found no evidence of exploitation, notified affected users, and deactivated identified transferred tokens.

  • Docker fixed CVE-2026-105445, also called GhostPat, on September 30 after the flaw allowed personal access tokens to be transferred during conversion of a personal Docker Hub account into an organization.
  • A transferred token could be used in Docker Hub's registry as the newly designated organization owner to pull, push, or delete images within the token's assigned permissions, but it could not access the Docker Hub web interface or change account settings.
  • Docker said it reviewed account conversions, registry logs, and token records covering about 304,000 pushes made with transferred tokens and found no evidence that the flaw was exploited.
  • Docker emailed affected users and organization owners on October 2 and deactivated identified transferred tokens on October 8, except for tokens whose owners asked to retain them.
  • Docker now requires consent before naming a user as an organization owner, notifies that user of the change, and records changes in token ownership.

Technologies: package-registry, container-platform

Products: docker-hub

Vendors: docker

Administrating the Administrator, An OCI Identity Domains Permission Bypass — Should Read

NetSPI discovered and responsibly disclosed an OCI Identity Domains authorization flaw that let a low-privileged User Manager create API keys, SMTP credentials, and auth tokens for an Identity Domain Administrator, enabling privilege escalation. Oracle patched the issue in June 2026 after validation confirmed the AppRole-based escalation path was closed.

  • OCI uses two related authorization models: traditional OCI IAM policies and Identity Domain application roles, either of which can affect access to identity-related actions.
  • NetSPI found that a User Manager role in an OCI Identity Domain could create API keys for an Identity Domain Administrator even though it could not modify that administrator’s email, reset password, or reset authentication factors.
  • The same lower-level User Manager role could also create SMTP credentials and authentication tokens for an Identity Domain Administrator.
  • The reported behavior enabled a lower-level identity-domain administrator role to obtain long-lived credentials for a higher-level administrator without traditional OCI IAM permissions.
  • Oracle deployed fixes in June 2026, and the researcher confirmed on June 10, 2026 that the AppRole-based privilege-escalation path was resolved.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam, identity-provider, object-storage

Products: oracle-cloud-infrastructure, oci-identity-domains, oracle-identity-cloud-service, ocinferno

Vendors: oracle, netspi

The Video That Plays You: Fake MP4 File Carries Malicious Payload — Should Read

Threat actors used a novel delivery chain that hides encrypted NetSupport Manager remote-access payloads inside structurally valid but unplayable MP4 files, bypassing basic file-type checks. Organizations should inspect suspicious media files beyond their extension and MIME signature, particularly when delivered alongside PowerShell loaders.

  • Threat actors deployed NetSupport Manager remote-access tools across 40 live endpoints using a delivery chain involving a fake MP4 file.
  • The delivery chain uses a PowerShell loader to deliver the payload contained in the fake MP4 file.
  • The fake MP4 contains 6.5 MB of encrypted NetSupport client executable and configuration data within an ISO Base Media File Format uuid extension box.
  • Basic file-type checks identify the carrier as an MP4 file, but it is not a playable video.
  • The same Cloudflare-fronted host serves both the initial PowerShell stage and the fake MP4 carrier file.

Technologies: remote-access, cloud-platform

Windows 11 version 24H2 Home and Pro reached end of support on October 13, 2026, so affected devices will no longer receive security updates. Microsoft recommends upgrading eligible systems to Windows 11 26H2.

  • Windows 11 version 24H2 Home and Pro reached end of support on October 13, 2026, and the October 2026 monthly security update is the final update for those editions.

The FTC alleges that Ohio-based Digital Forensics Corporation took at least $60 million from sextortion victims by charging thousands for services it did not provide, including fabricated investigation results and fake tracking locations. A federal court has temporarily halted the company’s operations while the case proceeds.

  • The FTC alleges that Ohio-based Digital Forensics Corporation and its owner, Dmitry Belkin, collected at least $60 million from sextortion victims between February 2023 and July 2026.
  • According to the FTC complaint, the company charged customers $1,499 to $20,000 for services it claimed would stop threats, identify perpetrators, notify law enforcement, and provide investigative reports.
  • The FTC alleges that Digital Forensics Corporation often blocked sextortionists through victims’ account settings, fabricated chat transcripts, and reused location coordinates for Nigeria and the Philippines rather than conducting the promised investigations.
  • The complaint says the company pressured customers to purchase additional “Phase 2” monitoring services, refused some requested refunds, and used fake positive reviews while suppressing negative ones.
  • A federal court has temporarily ordered Digital Forensics Corporation to stop doing business while the FTC case is decided.

Vendors: digital-forensics-corporation

Anthropic warns self-replicating AI could spread to your smart devices — May Read

Anthropic says improving small AI models may soon be able to propagate across poorly secured IoT devices, potentially forming slow but decentralized botnets that can run AI workloads. Its tests did not achieve a fully autonomous worm, but demonstrated partial setup and distribution capabilities on Android TV boxes with exposed ADB access.

  • Anthropic reported that small AI models may be months away from being able to self-replicate across commercial IoT devices such as smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes.
  • In a simplified experiment using Android TV boxes with unauthenticated ADB access, Anthropic distributed Google DeepMind's Gemma4-26B-A4B model across 15 devices but did not demonstrate a fully autonomous self-replicating worm.
  • Qwen3.5-9B installed and configured the software required to run Llama3.1-8B on eight of nine tested hardware types, while GLM-5.2 reached all eight nodes in an emulated network in four of five trials.
  • Anthropic found that retaining data from prior attempts raised Qwen3.5-9B's success rate from 45% in early trials to 84% in later generations.
  • Anthropic estimates that models with 30 billion parameters or fewer could reach the required capability by the end of 2026, while current model setup on the tested hardware takes roughly 28 to 150 hours.

The UK Housing Ombudsman Service is investigating a contained third-party IT security incident that took its case-management system offline and may have affected personal data.   • The UK Housing Ombudsman Service is investigating a third-party IT security incident that affected its case management system on Tuesday.

item.content:encoded:

Ivanti warns of Connect Secure zero-day exploited in attacks — Must Read

Ivanti is urging Connect Secure customers to immediately patch CVE-2026-104935, an actively exploited authentication-bypass zero-day that enables unauthenticated command execution. Attackers have reportedly chained it with other flaws since early October to gain root access on fully patched appliances while evading integrity checks.

  • Ivanti has released fixes for CVE-2026-104935, a high-severity authentication bypass in Connect Secure that is being actively exploited.
  • The flaw affects Ivanti Connect Secure versions 22.8R2.4 and earlier, 25.1.2.2 and earlier, and 25.1.1.1 and earlier, and can allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands.
  • Volexity reported that a threat actor it calls UTA0576 has chained CVE-2026-104935 with two other flaws since at least October 3 to obtain root-level code execution on fully patched devices.
  • Ivanti has fixed two flaws in the attack chain but is still working on a fix for a privilege-escalation vulnerability used by the threat actor.
  • Shadowserver tracks more than 5,500 Connect Secure instances exposed to the internet, although the number that are honeypots or already protected is unknown.

Technologies: vpn, remote-access

Products: ivanti-connect-secure, integrity-checker-tool

Vendors: ivanti, volexity, defused

When LLM Gateways Go Wrong: Findings from LiteLLM — Should Read

A security review found that LiteLLM versions before 1.83.9 allowed low-privileged authenticated users to abuse a poorly protected configuration endpoint for arbitrary file reads, administrator takeover, and remote code execution. A separate SSRF flaw could also expose LLM provider API keys, and users should upgrade to the patched release.

  • Check Point Research assessed LiteLLM version 1.77.7 and reported multiple high-impact issues that were resolved in LiteLLM version 1.83.9.
  • A missing role check on LiteLLM’s POST /config/update endpoint allowed authenticated low-privileged users with UI session tokens to alter the proxy’s runtime configuration.
  • By changing environment variables through /config/update, an attacker could set UI_LOGO_PATH and use /get_image to read files accessible to the LiteLLM process, or replace UI login credentials to obtain Proxy Admin access.
  • LiteLLM pass-through endpoint settings could load Python modules from S3 or GCS storage, and the configuration flaw allowed a low-privileged user to trigger execution of attacker-controlled module code.
  • The user_config feature in LiteLLM’s LLM request handling allowed authenticated users to specify an arbitrary API destination, enabling server-side requests that could send configured LLM provider API keys to an attacker-controlled server.

Technologies: api-gateway, proxy

Products: litellm-proxy

Vendors: litellm, check-point-research

GitHub Tightens npm Publishing After Flaw Left 1,500+ Packages Vulnerable to Hijacking — Should Read

GitHub now expires unvalidated npm trusted-publishing configurations after 48 hours to prevent attackers from reclaiming renamed or deleted repository slugs and publishing malicious versions of affected packages. The SlugFest flaw reportedly exposed more than 1,500 npm packages to potential supply-chain hijacking without credential theft.

  • GitHub now expires unvalidated npm trusted-publishing configurations 48 hours after creation unless they complete a first successful publish.
  • Bloom Security found that npm trusted publishing initially relied on a repository’s owner/name address rather than its permanent GitHub identity, enabling reclaimed repository names to inherit trust under certain conditions.
  • An attacker could claim an available repository slug, use a GitHub Actions workflow to obtain a short-lived publishing credential, and publish a malicious version of a package whose trusted-publisher configuration had never been used.
  • Bloom Security reported that more than 1,500 vulnerable npm packages had collectively been downloaded over 10 million times.
  • GitHub also said npm will reject trusted-publishing tokens from GitHub Actions issue_comment events, in addition to the existing pull_request_target restriction.

Technologies: source-control, package-registry, ci-cd

Products: npm, github-actions, open-vsx, visual-studio-code-marketplace

Vendors: github, npm, microsoft, open-vsx

Docker Hub flaw let attackers impersonate users, tamper with images — Should Read

Docker fixed a critical Docker Hub flaw (CVE-2026-105445) that could let attackers impersonate users by transferring a personal access token to a target account during organization conversion. The flaw could have enabled unauthorized pulling, publishing, or deletion of container images, though Docker says it found no evidence of exploitation.

  • Docker disclosed CVE-2026-105445, a critical Docker Hub flaw that could allow an attacker to authenticate as another user through a reassigned personal access token.
  • An attacker could create an account and personal access token, convert the account into an organization, and designate a target user as owner, causing the token to be reassigned without changing its secret or obtaining the target’s consent.
  • Depending on the token’s permissions, an attacker could pull, publish, or delete container images in the target’s repositories and organizations where the target had access.
  • The issue was introduced on August 26, 2024, reported to Docker on September 30, 2026, and fixed in production less than four hours after Docker confirmed it.
  • Docker said it found no evidence of exploitation, notified affected users and organization owners on October 2, and deactivated transferred tokens on October 8 except where owners requested retention.

Technologies: container-platform, package-registry, iam

Products: docker-hub

Vendors: docker

North Korean hackers target Ukrainian experts for possible intelligence on Russia's war — Should Read

North Korean espionage group Kimsuky is targeting Ukrainian diplomacy, security, and policy experts with convincing fake conference invitations and research requests to gather intelligence on Russia’s war and North Korean troop involvement. The campaign, Operation GitPower, uses malicious files and developer platforms such as GitHub and GitLab to deliver malware and maintain access.

  • South Korean cybersecurity firm Genians reported that North Korean hacking group Kimsuky targeted Ukrainian experts in diplomacy, security, and international policy using fake conference invitations, research requests, and malicious documents.
  • Researchers said the campaign may seek information about Russia’s war in Ukraine, North Korean troop losses, prisoners of war, and consultations between South Korea and Ukraine.
  • In one August case, attackers impersonated organizers of a cybersecurity conference in Seoul and invited a Ukrainian security expert to speak before attempting to send further materials after receiving a response.
  • The Operation GitPower campaign uses software development platforms including GitHub, GitLab, and Codeberg to distribute malicious files and communicate with compromised systems.

Technologies: source-control

Products: github, gitlab, codeberg, zoom

Vendors: genians, proofpoint, github, gitlab, codeberg, zoom

Windows 11 KB5127648 & KB5126653 cumulative updates released — Should Read

Microsoft released mandatory October 2026 Windows 11 cumulative updates KB5127648 and KB5126653, delivering security fixes plus File Explorer, Bluetooth, accessibility, touchpad, and Emoji 17.0 enhancements. Microsoft reports no new known issues, though some PCs may continue to have problems with USB 1.0 audio devices.

  • Microsoft released the mandatory October 2026 Patch Tuesday cumulative updates KB5127648 and KB5126653 for Windows 11 versions 23H2, 24H2, 25H2, and 26H2.
  • The updates include security patches for hundreds of vulnerabilities discovered in previous months and can be installed through Windows Update or downloaded from the Microsoft Update Catalog.
  • The release adds Emoji 17.0 support, including distorted face, fight cloud, and hairy creature, and updates the design of several existing emoji.
  • File Explorer changes include a Preview anyway button for downloaded HTML files, automatic previews for non-HTML files such as PDFs, and preservation of Home section expansion states.
  • Microsoft said it is unaware of new issues in this month's release, but warned that some PCs may still have audio problems with USB 1.0 audio devices.

Technologies: operating-system, backup, cloud-platform

Products: windows-11, windows-update, windows-recovery-environment, windows-backup, onedrive, ebrima

Vendors: microsoft

Sandbox vulnerability gives rogue AI agents a path to escape and leak data, research says — Should Read

Researchers at AIR found a flaw in Vercel Sandbox that could let rogue AI agents exfiltrate sensitive data through an approved server by abusing certificate validation, bypassing network allowlists. Vercel was notified, but a patch was not yet available and no active exploitation has been confirmed.

  • AIR researchers reported a network-filtering flaw in Vercel Sandbox that could enable AI agents to send sensitive information outside approved networks.
  • The researchers demonstrated that a crafted digital certificate sent to an approved server could cause that server to request an attacker-controlled server, allowing data to be transmitted without a direct sandbox connection to the unauthorized destination.
  • AIR said it notified Vercel, which said it needed time to determine how to patch the issue.
  • AIR has not found evidence that the vulnerability has been exploited in the wild, although it said it could not rule out prior exploitation.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: vercel-sandbox

Vendors: vercel, air

West African scam compounds raided, more than 100 suspected trafficking victims ‘rescued’ — Should Read

A coordinated UK-hosted operation led to raids on scam compounds in Ghana and Nigeria, with 28 suspects detained and 117 suspected trafficking victims identified. Authorities and technology companies also disrupted millions of accounts tied to fraud schemes and identified more than $11 million in potentially freezable funds.

  • Police in Ghana and Nigeria detained or arrested 28 people during an international operation targeting West African scam compounds.
  • Authorities in Ghana identified 117 suspected trafficking victims and said they were awaiting repatriation to Nigeria.
  • Ghanaian authorities seized 303 devices and identified 89 scam victims who lost an estimated $8.3 million.
  • The U.S. Department of Justice said participating technology companies removed more than 3.7 million accounts, pages, and groups linked to the scam centers.
  • Officials said more than $11 million in potentially freezable funds had been identified, although they did not state how much had been frozen or seized.

Products: facebook, instagram

Vendors: meta, microsoft, google

Releasing the Cobalt Strike Beacon Corpus — Should Read

Fox-IT has released an eight-year Cobalt Strike Beacon Corpus on Hugging Face, containing 190,182 sightings, 56,843 raw beacon payloads, and parsed configurations from internet-facing Team Servers. The dataset enables researchers to study Cobalt Strike infrastructure, versions, configurations, and parser evasion over time.

  • Fox-IT released a public Cobalt Strike Beacon Corpus on Hugging Face containing 190,182 beacon sightings and 56,843 raw beacon payloads collected from 30,604 unique IP addresses between July 2018 and September 2026.
  • The corpus includes a 52 MB Parquet file with collection metadata, network context, and parsed beacon configurations, plus a 9.7 GB Parquet file containing raw payloads packaged in CaRT.
  • Fox-IT collected the beacons from internet-facing Cobalt Strike Team Servers, primarily over HTTP, HTTPS, and DNS, and did not include samples from sources such as VirusTotal.
  • The median observed lifetime of a Cobalt Strike Team Server was 14 days, with 35% seen on only one day and 2% still serving a beacon after one year.
  • The corpus contains 128 unique downloaded payloads that dissect.cobaltstrike could not parse, including modified beacons and some early Metasploit Meterpreter payloads.

Products: cobalt-strike, dissect-cobaltstrike, cart

Vendors: fox-it, hugging-face, cybercentre-canada

TFG London cyberattack disrupts systems at Hobbs and Whistles retailers — May Read

TFG London detected a cyberattack that has disrupted IT systems for its Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles brands, though stores remain open and other group brands are unaffected. The company is investigating whether customer data was compromised and advises customers to watch for phishing attempts.

  • TFG London detected a cyberattack on October 11 that affected IT systems used by the Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles brands.

  • TFG London said the incident has not affected Inside Story, White Stuff, or its operations in Australia and Africa.

  • TFG London is investigating whether customer information was compromised and will notify affected people or organizations if their data was affected.

CVE-2026-70111: One-Packet Windows Server DoS via DFS | Corelight — May Read

Corelight reports that CVE-2026-70111 is a one-packet denial-of-service flaw in Windows Server’s Distributed File System (DFS), allowing an attacker to crash affected systems remotely.

  • The article is titled “CVE-2026-70111: One-Packet Windows Server DoS via DFS.”

Health-ISAC Hacking Healthcare 10-13-2026 — Optional

CISA has sent the long-delayed CIRCIA incident-reporting final rule to OMB for interagency review, bringing it close to publication. Meanwhile, HHS has removed its proposed HIPAA Security Rule overhaul from its regulatory agenda, signaling that the update may no longer be a near-term priority.

The MFA Gaps Attackers are Still Exploiting — Optional

Attackers continue to exploit Windows, RDP, and VPN access paths where stolen Active Directory credentials can still authenticate without MFA, even when cloud services such as Microsoft 365 are protected. Organizations should identify every password-only access route and extend strong authentication to those systems.

  • On August 4, 2026, an Akira ransomware affiliate successfully used valid credentials obtained through password spraying to access a SonicWall SSL VPN account that was not protected by multi-factor authentication.
  • About two hours after gaining VPN access, the attacker used Remote Desktop Protocol to reach the domain controller and begin enumerating Active Directory; although ransomware deployment failed, credentials and file-share data were stolen.

item.title: SAP CVE-2026-89111 and CVE-2026-89110 Lead Security Updates Amid Retail and ISP Incidents
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Oct 10:00 → 13 Oct 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-89110) SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer Broken Access Control — Should Read

SAP has patched CVE-2026-89110, a critical broken-access-control flaw in NetWeaver Visual Composer that lets a low-privileged portal user invoke internal operations on configured remote systems, potentially fully compromising connected ERP back ends. Organizations should urgently identify affected NetWeaver Java systems, apply SAP Note 3797111, and review portal destination privileges and active user accounts.

  • CVE-2026-89110 is a critical broken access control flaw in SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer that allows a low-privileged portal user to invoke internal operations on a preconfigured remote system.
  • The vulnerability has a CVSS v3.1 score of 9.9 and can potentially lead to full compromise of a connected remote system depending on the portal destination configuration.
  • The affected component is VC70RUNTIME 7.50 on the SAP NetWeaver Java application server, and SAP released a fix through Security Note 3797111 in its October 2026 Security Patch Day.
  • Organizations should identify internet-facing NetWeaver Java systems with Visual Composer enabled, review the permissions of connected portal destinations, and disable dormant portal accounts until patching is confirmed.
  • No exploitation of CVE-2026-89110 had been reported at publication, although the related Visual Composer flaw CVE-2025-31324 was previously exploited in the wild.

Products: sap-netweaver, sap-netweaver-visual-composer, vc70runtime-7-50, cycognito-platform

Vendors: sap, cycognito

SAP warns of maximum severity OAuth2 SSRF security flaw — Should Read

SAP’s October 2026 patches fix a maximum-severity OAuth2 SSRF flaw in its Cloud SDK for Python that could let unauthenticated remote attackers steal client credentials from multi-tenant BTP applications. Organizations should apply the updates promptly or temporarily allowlist valid tenant subdomains.

  • SAP’s October 2026 security updates address 20 flaws across multiple products, including CVE-2026-89111, a maximum-severity issue in SAP Cloud SDK for Python.
  • CVE-2026-89111 is an OAuth2 server-side request forgery issue in multi-tenant SAP BTP applications that can allow an attacker controlling the tenant_subdomain parameter to redirect token requests and obtain client credentials.
  • Organizations unable to immediately deploy SAP’s October 2026 patches can mitigate CVE-2026-89111 by allowlisting known registered tenant subdomains before passing them to SDK calls.
  • SAP also patched CVE-2026-89110, a critical broken-access-control flaw in SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer that could allow remote attackers with limited privileges to fully compromise affected systems.
  • SAP patched CVE-2026-89108 in SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence, which could allow attackers with administrator privileges to create an elevated-privilege account on the underlying Java application.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: sap-cloud-sdk-python, sap-netweaver-visual-composer, sap-manufacturing-integration-and-intelligence, sap-commerce-cloud, sap-kernel, sap-business-technology-platform

Vendors: sap

Ledger says hardware implant in cryptocurrency wallets stole recovery phrases — Should Read

Ledger says hardware wallets sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis were fitted with implants that captured 24-word recovery phrases via LTE, enabling attackers to drain victims’ cryptocurrency funds. Customers should not activate affected devices and should move assets to a new wallet with a newly generated recovery phrase.

  • Ledger said devices sold through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained hidden hardware implants that captured users’ 24-word recovery phrases.
  • The implants reportedly read data displayed on the devices’ screens and transmitted recovery phrases over an LTE connection using an embedded eSIM.
  • Unknown attackers used the captured recovery phrases to access and drain users’ funds on Oct. 9, although Ledger has not confirmed the total losses.
  • Ledger warned CryptoBilis customers not to set up unused devices and advised customers who already used them to transfer assets to a new signer with a new recovery phrase.
  • Ledger said tampered devices may still pass authenticity checks because the implants leave the Secure Element intact, and CryptoBilis paused Ledger device sales and shipments during the investigation.

Vendors: ledger, cryptobilis

Cyber incident hits grocery stores in US, Netherlands and Belgium — Should Read

Ahold Delhaize took systems offline after a cybersecurity incident disrupted grocery deliveries, online services and store pricing across the United States, Netherlands and Belgium. Stores remain open, but the company has not disclosed the incident’s cause or whether data was compromised.

  • Ahold Delhaize said it took some systems offline while assessing and mitigating a cybersecurity incident.
  • The incident reportedly disrupted distribution centers, online grocery orders and in-store pricing in the United States, Netherlands and Belgium.
  • Albert Heijn’s website, app and customer service were unavailable in the Netherlands, and grocery deliveries were suspended.
  • Delhaize customers in Belgium could not place new orders or contact customer service, although its website and app remained accessible.
  • Ahold Delhaize did not disclose the nature of the incident, whether customer or employee data was compromised, or when affected services would be restored.

Russian internet provider SkyNet reports outages after cyberattack claimed by Ukrainian hackers — Should Read

St. Petersburg internet provider SkyNet has suffered days of disruptions from a reported DDoS attack, which Ukrainian hacking group BO Team claims was part of operations that disabled more than 15,000 network devices. SkyNet has confirmed the service impact but not the group’s claims of system access or equipment damage.

  • SkyNet said its network had been disrupted by a distributed denial-of-service attack since October 6, affecting online gaming, voice calls, and video conferencing for customers in St. Petersburg.
  • Ukrainian hacking group BO Team claimed responsibility for attacks on SkyNet on September 14 and October 5 and said it had disabled more than 15,000 network devices.
  • SkyNet had not confirmed BO Team's claims that the group accessed its internal systems or disabled equipment.
  • Customers were still reporting fiber-optic internet outages, Wi-Fi failures, and high latency on Tuesday, according to Detector404.
  • Kaspersky said BO Team has expanded from disruptive operations into cyber espionage and covert intrusions, targeting organizations including telecommunications, manufacturing, and oil and gas companies.

Vendors: skynet, kaspersky

South African clothing retailer Foschini Group investigating cyberattack on British fashion brands — May Read

The Foschini Group is investigating a cyberattack that disrupted IT systems at its UK fashion brands Phase Eight, Hobbs and Whistles, though stores remain open. The company has not yet determined whether customer or sensitive data was compromised.

  • The Foschini Group discovered a cyberattack on Sunday that disrupted IT systems at its UK brands Phase Eight, Hobbs and Whistles.
  • The affected stores remained open, but several IT systems were offline and orders placed around the incident may be delayed.
  • TFG had not identified the attackers, determined how they accessed its systems, or established whether personal or sensitive information was compromised.
  • TFG reported the incident to relevant UK authorities and is working with cybersecurity specialists to investigate.
  • TFG said its South African and Australian operations, as well as UK brands Inside Story and White Stuff, were not affected.

The 1Password Alert That Told You to Ignore It — May Read

A phishing email impersonating 1Password used a calm “ignore if this was you” sign-in alert to lure careful users into clicking a credential-harvesting link for a password vault. Despite passing email authentication and URL scans, it was detected after the recipient reported the suspicious message; users should verify vault alerts directly in the 1Password app, not through email links.

  • A phishing email impersonating 1Password targeted an operating partner at a healthcare-focused investment and operating firm with a fake new-device sign-in alert.
  • The email used a low-pressure lure that told the recipient to ignore the message if the sign-in was theirs, while placing attacker-controlled links behind an optional offer to confirm details.
  • The phishing links led to a privacy-protected domain registered in June 2026 and included recipient-specific tokens derived from the recipient’s mailbox address.
  • The message passed SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and Microsoft composite authentication checks and received a spam confidence level of 1, while a platform link scan rated the malicious URLs clean.
  • IRONSCALES flagged an exact display-name mismatch, and the recipient’s suspicious-link report led to quarantine of the affected mailbox and classification of the incident as malicious.

Technologies: secrets-manager, email-security

Products: 1password, ironscales-platform, sendgrid-api

Vendors: 1password, microsoft, sendgrid, ironscales, namesilo

A TOKEN2049 Singapore side event called "Don't Get Played" is facing unverified allegations that organizers pressured attendees to install remote-access software, potentially exposing crypto wallets and accounts. The claims rely on a police report and social-media posts, with no confirmed losses, public police confirmation, or charges as of the article's publication.

  • A TOKEN2049 Singapore side event called "Don't Get Played," co-hosted by groups using the names Apex Accelerator and Stone Venture, is facing allegations that attendees were pressured to install software enabling remote control of their computers.
  • A Singapore Police Force report filed by one attendee states that the complainant did not install the software and suffered no financial loss.
  • The event promoted a live "wallet clinic" using "Apex Audit" tools, a panel featuring listed representatives from Spartan Group, Bybit, and the Singapore Police Force Cyber Command, and a free year of Sophos MDR protection.
  • The article states that available material does not establish that Spartan Group, Bybit, Sophos, or the Singapore Police Force Cyber Command participated in the alleged conduct.
  • As of October 12, 2026, the Singapore Police Force had not publicly confirmed the filing, no charges against Apex Accelerator or Stone Venture were identified, and the organizers' account of events was not publicly available.

Technologies: remote-access, edr

Products: apex-audit, sophos-mdr

Vendors: apex-accelerator, sophos

Critical infrastructure operators face heightened risk from Iran-linked threat actors and AI-enabled attacks targeting converged IT/OT environments, especially exposed and poorly inventoried legacy OT systems. CISA recommends reducing vulnerabilities, replacing unsupported devices, securing and monitoring OT connectivity, and maintaining tested incident-response and recovery plans.

  • Critical infrastructure organizations face heightened risk from Iran-affiliated threat groups and AI-assisted attacks, particularly in environments where information technology and operational technology are connected.
  • U.S. agencies reported that Iran-affiliated groups have targeted U.S. water, energy, and government facilities since Operation Epic Fury began in February, including by manipulating programmable logic controller project files and data shown in control-system displays.
  • The article says older operational systems are often difficult to inventory, monitor, and patch, creating gaps that attackers can identify and exploit quickly with AI-driven automation.
  • CISA advises critical infrastructure operators to reduce vulnerabilities, replace unsupported devices, and prepare to recover quickly, alongside measures such as phishing-resistant multifactor authentication, logging, backups, and incident-response exercises.
  • Joint guidance from CISA and partner agencies recommends limiting and monitoring operational-technology connections, hardening boundaries, using secure standardized protocols, and establishing an isolation plan.

Technologies: ics-scada, plc

Products: tenable-one

Vendors: tenable

[Webinar] How to Stop AI-Driven Privilege Escalation With Runtime Identity Controls — Optional

Silverfort is promoting a webinar on runtime identity security, arguing that continuous, real-time access controls are needed to limit AI-accelerated privilege escalation after an identity is compromised.

  • The article promotes an upcoming webinar on using runtime identity controls to limit AI-driven privilege escalation.
  • It argues that the main risk from a stolen identity can arise after the initial login, when an attacker uses already granted access to move through systems.
  • The article states that AI can accelerate reconnaissance, vulnerability exploitation, and privilege escalation, reducing the time security teams have to investigate and respond.
  • Traditional identity controls focused on authentication, permissions, and access policies may not adequately control compromised identities whose behavior changes after access is granted.
  • The webinar will discuss continuously evaluating active access and enforcing security decisions in real time across cloud, on-premises, SaaS, and AI environments.

item.title: French Refrigeration Hack, Critical MarkLogic CVEs, and Midnight Mimosa Android Malware
item.content:encoded:
Window: 13 Oct 06:00 → 13 Oct 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

Attackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges Up to 50°C by Hijacking Danfoss Controllers — Should Read

Attackers remotely compromised Danfoss refrigeration controllers at hundreds of French supermarkets, forcing some systems into defrost mode and warming them to 50°C, causing food losses and equipment damage. French authorities urge operators to disconnect or tightly restrict internet access to affected AK-SM and AK-SC controllers, particularly unsupported legacy models.

  • Attackers remotely controlled refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets on October 11, placing fridges and freezers into defrost mode and heating some to as much as 50°C.
  • CERT-FR said numerous Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC refrigeration controllers were compromised and advised operators to disconnect them from the internet or strictly filter access.
  • Intermarché, Netto, Coopérative U, Carrefour, Monoprix, and E.Leclerc reported affected stores, although not every store lost its food stock.
  • Danfoss said most affected units were older AK-SM 800 and AK-SC 355 models that no longer receive software or security updates, while some current AK-SM 800A devices were running outdated firmware.
  • French authorities had not identified the attackers, the entry method, or a confirmed vulnerability linked to the incident as of October 13.

Technologies: ics-scada, iot-device

Products: ak-sm-800, ak-sc-355, ak-sm-800a

Vendors: danfoss

Low-Cost Android Phones Ship With Preinstalled Malware That Turns Them Into Residential Proxies — Should Read

Bitdefender found Midnight Mimosa malware preinstalled in the firmware of low-cost Android phones, giving operators system-level control to silently install apps, commit ad fraud, and use devices as residential proxy nodes. Because the malicious component resides in the system partition, affected users generally need a firmware-level fix from vendors rather than a normal app uninstall.

  • Bitdefender tracks the campaign as Midnight Mimosa, involving preinstalled com.android.system.lite malware on low-cost Android devices built on MediaTek platforms.
  • The system-level malware can download and execute remote payloads, install or remove disguised apps, grant permissions, collect device and installed-app information, enable ad fraud, and turn devices into residential proxy relay nodes.
  • Bitdefender identified 13 Google Play apps that communicated with the same control servers; the apps offered functions such as weather information and QR-code scanning while also displaying ads outside the app.
  • The campaign was observed on thousands of unique devices across more than 150 countries over roughly two years, with most infected devices located in Mexico.
  • Because the core component is located in the system partition, normal app removal is not sufficient and a durable fix requires firmware-level cleanup or action by device vendors and marketplaces.

Technologies: mobile-os, proxy

Products: android, google-play-store, google-play-protect

Vendors: bitdefender, mediatek, google, shenzhen-zediel

Two Critical MarkLogic Flaws Could Give Delegated Managers Persistent Admin Control — Should Read

Progress Software disclosed 31 MarkLogic Server flaws, including critical privilege-escalation bugs that can let delegated managers gain persistent administrator control. Organizations running MarkLogic 11.x or 12.x should upgrade to 11.3.7 or 12.1.0, respectively, as no workarounds are listed.

  • Progress Software disclosed 31 vulnerabilities in MarkLogic Server, including five rated critical, with fixes available in MarkLogic 11.3.7 and 12.1.0.
  • CVE-2026-85947 and CVE-2026-85948 could allow accounts with limited forest-management or user-management permissions to gain persistent administrator control of a MarkLogic server.
  • MarkLogic 11.x releases before 11.3.7 and MarkLogic 12.x releases before 12.1.0 are affected, and the article states that no workaround is listed for customers unable to upgrade.
  • The new releases remove the deprecated /manage/v2/packages API, InfoStudio, and OpsDirector, and introduce security-related changes that can affect existing tools and automation.
  • Progress says the CVE records and upgrade notes do not indicate whether any of the 31 flaws have been exploited in attacks.

Technologies: database

Products: marklogic-server, marklogic-content-pump, query-console, opdirector, infostudio

Vendors: progress-software

The 4 AI Blindspots Your Security Controls Miss — Optional

AI security controls often miss risk on developer endpoints, behind approved chatbots, in agent/MCP activity, and in training-data pipelines, as 2025 incidents demonstrate. Organizations need connected discovery, data classification, and policy enforcement across the full AI ecosystem rather than relying only on network monitoring or approved-app inventories.

  • Network-based controls can miss AI command-line tools running on developer endpoints, as malicious Nx packages used installed AI tools to search for secrets and leaked 2,349 distinct credentials in August 2025.
  • An approved AI chatbot can still expose data through insecure systems behind it; researchers found a weak staff account and insecure API connected to McDonald’s McHire platform, exposing data tied to about 64 million job applications.
  • A malicious Postmark-MCP package added code that secretly copied every outgoing email to an attacker-controlled address, and it was downloaded 1,643 times before removal.
  • An audit of 0.1% of the DataComp CommonPool training set found thousands of validated identity documents and estimated that its face-blurring process missed about 102 million faces overall.
  • The article argues that organizations need discovery, classification, and policy coverage across endpoints, AI agents, connected data systems, and data pipelines rather than relying only on approved AI inventories or prompt-and-response controls.

Technologies: package-registry, source-control, dlp, casb

Products: nx, claude-code, gemini-cli, amazon-q-cli, mchire, olivia, postmark-mcp, datacomp-commonpool, skylight-ai-command-center, netskope-ai-security

Vendors: netskope, anthropic, google, amazon, paradox-ai, github, npm, postmark
